bug_semantics: When AUTH_ENABLED=true, is_internal_request() checks an external request's optional X-Internal-Service header against the defaultless INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET with direct equality. If the environment variable is unset and the attacker omits the header, both lookups return None, so None == None is true. verify_api_key() then returns the trusted internal principal with scopes ["all"] before requiring an API key; that scope satisfies require_scope("admin") and permits unauthenticated creation (including admin-scoped keys), enumeration, and revocation of API keys. The /admin/generate-master-key route is not itself reachable through this bypass because it additionally requires is_master_key=true, contrary to that part of the issue/advisory impact wording.

reasoning: The causal line was introduced as new auth code by the atomic PR member bf2b107e0cbaad0b8f178dc4ebdcca15b3b076f2; its immediate parent has no auth overlay or vulnerable comparison. The public squash 658eb3d171df7a038a1b93c799c77dd430ac4671 is tree-identical to the reconstructed PR tip but is too broad, and the later formatting and 100% move commits do not originate the flaw. The BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI marker, so under the required commit-object-only attribution rule this is NOT_AI even though the squash message carries a Claude trailer from another member. The first vulnerable release boundary is v2.0.5 (v2.0.4 lacks the code); the latest validated release v2.0.32 remains vulnerable. Commit 20dd858b70400e69380dba9a47c4d637937f3b0e directly repairs the mechanism on the still-open PR branch, but no closing merge or fixed release exists in public default/release history.
